transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, what brought me in today is... I had an incident recently where I really lost my temper. I blew up at one of the younger volunteers where I help out, and it was just over a crooked tablecloth. 

It was completely uncalled for. I don't usually talk to people that way, so it didn't sit right with me. I figured I should come in and talk to somebody about what's going on.
Has this kind of incident happened to you before?

No, not really. I've never been the type to just snap at people like that. This... well, this whole thing has only been going on for about a week. It all started right after that robbery outside the bank.
Have you been having any repetitive thoughts or urges to do something over and over since the incident started?

No, I can't say that I have. I don't have any urges to do things over and over, if that's what you mean. It's really just been... well, just feeling a bit short-tempered like I mentioned. But no, no repetitive thoughts or anything like that.
Has this short-temperedness been causing you significant distress or problems in your daily life?

Yes, it has been causing some issues. I mean, I usually do a lot of the organizing for the local Día de los Muertos event, but... well, I just haven't been able to keep up with it the way I normally do. 

And I've actually stopped going to my regular card nights, too. I just don't feel very steady around people right now, so it's definitely getting in the way of my normal routine.
Are you avoiding places or situations that remind you of the robbery outside the bank?

Yes, I am. I've actually been taking the long way around when I go out, just so I don't have to pass by that bank. And... well, I haven't gone into the festival storage room either. It just brings the whole thing a little too close for comfort right now.
Are you avoiding the people you yelled at or any other social interactions because of fear of losing your temper again?

No, I wouldn't say I'm avoiding people specifically because I'm afraid I'll yell at them. I mean, I feel bad about snapping at my family, but I'm not hiding from them or anything. It's more just... I don't feel up to being in a big group right now, like at card night. But it's not because I'm worried about my temper, it's just that I don't feel steady.
Have you noticed any changes in how you interact with your family or close friends since this incident started?

Not really, no. I mean, aside from what I just mentioned about snapping at them a couple of times, and... well, skipping my card games. But other than that, no, I haven't noticed any big changes. We still talk and do our usual things around the house. I'm just maybe a little quieter than usual, but that's about it.
Are you avoiding social situations because you're worried about losing control of your emotions again?

Well, like I was saying just a minute ago... no. It's really not about being worried I'll lose control of my emotions. I'm just sitting out on things like card night because I don't feel quite settled yet, not because I'm afraid I'll blow up or get emotional with anybody.
Have you been feeling anxious a lot since the robbery happened?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling anxious a lot. I mean... obviously it shook me up when it happened, but I'm not sitting around worrying or feeling nervous all day. Like I said before, I just feel a little unsteady right now, but I wouldn't really call it anxiety.
Are you avoiding the festival storage room because it reminds you of the robbery?

Yeah, I guess so. I just... I haven't gone in there because it brings the whole thing back, makes it feel a bit too close, you know? And honestly, I've even been taking the long way around town so I don't have to walk past the bank. It's just easier to avoid those places for now.
Have you been feeling less emotionally responsive or numb since the robbery happened?

No, I wouldn't say I feel numb. I mean, my emotions are still there... I still feel things normally. I'm just, like I said, feeling a little unsettled. But I haven't noticed any kind of blankness or feeling disconnected from my emotions.
Do you feel disconnected from the people around you?
No, I wouldn't say that. I'm still talking to my family and friends just the same as always. I don't feel cut off from anybody, if that's what you mean. I'm doing fine with the people around me.
Do you find yourself constantly thinking or worrying about the robbery that happened outside the bank?

No, not constantly. I mean, it pops into my head sometimes, especially if I'm near the bank like I mentioned, but I'm not sitting around dwelling on it all day. I'm not really worrying about it happening again or anything like that. It's just a bad memory, but it's not taking over my thoughts.
Are there any other places, activities, or things that you're avoiding because they remind you of the robbery?

Well, I have been taking the long way around when I go into town, just so I don't have to pass by that bank. And... I haven't gone into the festival storage room at the community center lately. It just, I don't know, it brings the whole thing a bit too close to mind, so I've just been staying clear of it.
Are there any other activities or places you've been avoiding since the robbery happened?
No, that's really it. Just the bank and the storage room. I haven't been avoiding anything else that I can think of.
Do you often find yourself thinking about the robbery when you don't want to?

Well, yeah, sometimes I do. Like I said, I'm not dwelling on it on purpose, but... well, out of nowhere, I'll just hear that man's rough voice in my head. Or I'll see the donation envelope hitting the ground again. And this happens even when I'm just sitting quietly at my kitchen table, not thinking about the town or the bank at all. It just kind of forces its way in.
Are there any other memories or reminders of the robbery that you're trying to avoid thinking about?

No, not really. I mean, I try not to think about the whole thing in general, but there aren't any specific memories I'm trying to push away, other than what I've already mentioned. It's just those flashes that pop up.
Are there any other memories or reminders of the robbery that you're trying to avoid?
Well, like I just mentioned a second ago, no, I don't think so. There really isn't anything else I'm going out of my way to avoid. Just the things we already went over.
Are you making an effort to avoid thinking about the robbery itself?

Well, no, not really. I'm not sitting around forcing myself to block it out or anything. I just... I try to go about my normal day. If the thought pops up, it pops up, but I'm not making some special effort to avoid thinking about the robbery itself. I'm just living my life as best I can.
